title: Iron Man suit that can fly
objective: Design an Iron Man suit that can fly
spoken: Simulation Lab for Iron Man suit that can fly, sir. I screened 2,320 candidate designs with equations, which are mathematical predictions, not simulations, and ran 10,000 Monte Carlo simulations on the strongest 10. Closest realistic solution, electric hover flight for one person: total fan disk area 1.4 m², battery mass 65 kg, battery pack specific energy 290 Wh/kg, motor specific power 6.6 kW/kg. Hover time: about 12 minutes, between 9.9 minutes and 13 minutes; it met every constraint in 100% of runs. Estimated cost about $18,338. Eliminated 1,163: mostly more than 1.5 m² of fans, too large to wear, then the battery would have to discharge faster than 10C. These are simulated results, not measurements: nothing has been built or tested. Crewed flight can kill. Any test starts unmanned, tethered and subscale, under the aviation authority's rules.
roadmap: Check the hover model against a small tethered fan rig (thrust and power measured, unmanned).
Build a subscale unmanned demonstrator and measure hover time.
Full-size tethered, unmanned test with a dummy load.
Crewed flight only with certified parts, the regulator and a professional test programme.
